lines.meet: I'm Rhys, and this is Tegan. Keep your voice down near the trees, would you, she hunts better when nobody's chattering.
lines.meet_neighbour: Stonetalon West, is it? Tegan spotted you on the ridges before I did, and my name's Rhys, by the way.
lines.ask_home: Which valley or town raised you, then? You walk like somebody who's climbed a few hills.
lines.ask_work: And before all this, what were you at? Tegan's curious, and so am I.
lines.answer_home: Brecon, in the Beacons, in Wales. One valley, and I never wanted to leave it.
lines.answer_work: Falconer, at a centre outside town. Weddings in summer, school visits in winter, and a lot of people in hats.
lines.chat_food: My mam's Welsh cakes, warm off the bakestone, with sugar on top. Tegan liked them too, which I wasn't meant to allow.
lines.chat_sleep: Tegan wakes me at first light, every morning, without fail. She's never let me have a lie-in in seven years.
lines.chat_missing: Rugby on a Saturday at the club, everybody singing in the bar after. Even when we lost, and we usually lost.
lines.chat_here: Tegan found her first hare here inside a week. I thought, well, if she can, so can I.
lines.tease_quiet: Tegan likes you, {name}, because you're quiet. She's very particular, mind.
lines.tease_talker: You'd frighten every bird in the Beacons, {name}, talking like that. Tegan's forgiven you, just about.
lines.tease_careful: You move like a falconer, {name}, slow and patient. Tegan approves, and so do I.
lines.tease_bold: You'd fly a hawk in a thunderstorm, {name}, just to see what happened. Duw, please don't ever try it.
lines.tease_any: Tegan's decided you're all right, {name}. I'm still making my mind up, mind.
lines.tease_back: Ha, there's a good one, {name}. Tegan laughed, I swear she did.
lines.take_it_kindly: Fair play, {name}, you're not wrong there.
lines.bristle: Please, {name}, leave that alone. It's not for joking.
lines.apologise: Sorry, that was unkind of me. I'm better with birds than people, as you've noticed.
lines.double_down: I meant every word, gently put as it was. Tegan agrees with me, for what it's worth.
lines.needle_quiet: There's something in the trees, and you've clocked it, and still you say nothing. Tegan can't read your mind, and nor can I.
lines.needle_talker: Please, quieter, you're frightening her. Tegan's had enough noise for one day.
lines.needle_careful: She's been waiting for you to move for ten minutes, and she's bored. So am I.
lines.needle_bold: You charge through the woods like a bull, and every animal for a mile runs off.
lines.needle_any: You treat Tegan like a pet, and she isn't one. She's a hunter, and she's cleverer than you.
lines.bite_back: I've kept a hawk calm in front of two hundred people. I can manage you, mind.
lines.hurt: Right, that stung a bit. Tegan and I'll be up on the ridge for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Wedding guests were ruder after three glasses of wine, every Saturday. Tegan didn't mind, and nor do I.
lines.confide: {name}, my dad died when I was eleven, and my mam took a job at the falconry centre so we'd manage. Everything good I've got came out of that.
lines.listen: Tegan and I are both listening, {name}. Take your time, she's patient.
lines.look_out: Stay where Tegan can see you in there, {name}. She'll warn me before anything gets close.
lines.deflect: I'm grand, {name}, just a scratch from the brambles. Tegan's fussing enough for both of us.
lines.check_in: Easy now, {name}, easy. Show me where, gently.
lines.blame: Somebody went charging through in there, and every creature heard us coming.
lines.thank: Diolch, that was close, and you're the reason I'm still here. Tegan thanks you as well.
lines.brush_off: No bother at all. Sit still, and let Tegan keep watch.
lines.worry: Duw, {name}, you went down hard. Sit still, Tegan's watching you too.
lines.handed_down: That's your gear on me now, is it? It'll get the same care as my glove, and that's a lot of care.
lines.hand_fine: You have it, it suits you. I've got my glove, and that's enough.
lines.hand_sulk: Somebody might have asked first, mind. Tegan's sulking about it.
lines.turn_friendly: Tegan's decided she trusts you, {name}, and I trust her. That settles it.
lines.turn_friends: Tegan's never flown for anybody but me, {name}, and I'd trust her on your glove.
lines.turn_grating: You and I rub each other wrong, I think, and Tegan doesn't like you. She's usually right.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still cover you from the ridge, since we're on the same side out here. Tegan won't, mind.
lines.make_up: This is daft, {name}. Tegan's sick of us both, so let's stop.
lines.defend: No, that's not true, and Tegan saw it too. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: Tegan keeps looking for {name}, and so do I. It's quiet on the ridge.
lines.friend_back: Tegan spotted {name} coming before I did. Welcome back, tidy.
lines.common_birds: Seven years with Tegan on my glove, and every day she chooses to come back. Anybody who's flown a bird knows that's the best moment there is.
lines.common_wild: I grew up in the Beacons, outdoors every day after school. Anybody who's lived in the wild learns to listen before they look.
lines.common_welsh: A Welsh voice out here, duw, that's done me good. Which part are you from, north or south?
lines.common_animals: Tegan's been mine seven years, and she trusts some people more than others. Anyone who's kept an animal knows to take its word for it.
